content:
Hi everyone! It is time to start drafting the Carleson formalization paper.

Each of the tasks below corresponds to drafting a (sub)section of the paper. Keep in mind that these are preliminary sections so that we can split the work, but some of them might be reorganized or combined later on.

Remember that whatever you write in the paper will likely get edited by others.

Tasks:

1 :new: 1.1. Brief history of Carleson’s theorem and significance
2 :play:(@María Inés de Frutos Fernández) 1.2. Overview of the formalization project
3 :new: 1.3. Related work
4 :play: (@Leo Diedering) 2.1. Mathematical background
5 :play: (@Jasper Mulder-Sohn) 2.2. Statement of the main results
6 :play: (@Floris van Doorn) 3. Project organization
7 :new: 4.1. The blueprint writing process
8 :new: 4.2. Changes and refinements
9 :new: 4.3. Dealing with mistakes
10 :new: 4.4. Lessons learned
11 :play: (@María Inés de Frutos Fernández) 5.1. Treatment of constants
12 :play: (@Sébastien Gouëzel) 5.2. The ProofData pattern
13 :play: (@Jim Portegies ) 5.3. Working with real numbers
14 :play: (@Michael Rothgang) 5.4. Use of ENorm
15 :new: 5.5. Working with Lp functions
16 :play: (@Joris Roos) 5.6. The BoundedCompactSupport structure
17 :new: 5.7. Common pitfalls
18 :new: 6. Conclusion
Thanks for posting this, Maria! @channel For the authors of the formalization: please contribute a subsection!
Can I take 12?

I could give 13 a try, if I understand what is meant there. I had my own experiences with the real numbers, but i also remember talks by Floris where he mentioned for instance suprema first taking values in the real numbers, but later switched to extended real numbers because it was quite inconvenient.
I volunteer for 16
Thank you to everyone who volunteered! I updated the list.

I can try to draft some parts of 4 (Mathematical background).
Maybe later I could also add something to 13 or 14 when @Jim Portegies resp. @Michael Rothgang are finished since I also had some experience with both of these topics (I think the switch to ENNReal was partly in response to my problems with suprema over the real numbers).

When I have a look at the sections still available, I think I could contribute the most to chapter 3 (if split to subsections is an option there). I'm also happy to review and add to other subsections when a first draft is available.
If chapter 3 is not available, I could try task 5 but I don't feel 100% confident about that.
Chapter 3 is taken by Floris, do you want to give task 5 a go? The blueprint should provide a good starting point for that.
Alright, I'll give task 5 a shot :thumbs_up:

I have just created carleson#526 with writing about blueprint changes related to the Hardy-Littlewood maximal function, the real interpolation theorem and the use of enorms. This completes task 14 and half of task 8. Comments welcome!

Hi all,

The Carleson project has seen a bit of a lull in the last months, but I would like to make sure we keep working on both the paper and porting our work to Mathlib.
Maybe we can try to set some deadlines to get things moving again, say in 3 weeks, on Friday April 24.

  • For the people that have claimed a paper writing task, could you submit a PR with your section by this deadline? If not, could you propose another self-imposed deadline yourself? (cc @Leo Diedering, @Jasper Mulder-Sohn, me, @Sébastien Gouëzel, @Jim Portegies, @Joris Roos)
  • There are still sections to claim. If you feel comfortable writing one of the unclaimed sections, please claim one.
  • If you do not feel comfortable writing one of the sections, please help with porting results to Mathlib: #Carleson > Porting to Mathlib
Friday April 24 is not too convenient for me, but I'll self-impose the deadline of Thursday, April 30 if that's ok.
I can claim task 1. I have split task 9 into subtasks: I can write about the mistakes in chapter 6 of the blueprint, but someone else will have to discuss the remaining issues.
I'll try to finish my section one of these days
My apologies, I'll be a few days late with this. I plan to finish it over the weekend
I can take up task 15 (L^p functions)
#554 completes task 15
Task 16: #557
Task 13: #558
Task 5: fpvandoorn/carleson#535
Task 12: fpvandoorn/carleson#561
I updated #558, thanks for the good suggestions @María Inés de Frutos Fernández !

CI on master has been failing on the "Generate the paper PDF" step since Carleson#558 because the new "Working with real numbers" subsection includes a literal ≠ in paper/main.tex, and pdflatex's default utf8 inputenc doesn't have a mapping for it...

Quick fix in Carleson#572: \DeclareUnicodeCharacter{2260}{\ensuremath{\neq}} in the preamble + switch the surrounding \texttt{...} to \lean{...} to match how every other Lean snippet in the paper is rendered.

Merged right now. It should work (tested locally)...
Thanks for the quick fix!
Yes, it worked https://github.com/fpvandoorn/carleson/actions/runs/25439038760
Thanks! Should we just use XeLaTeX as our TeX engine in CI? That works with minted, and last time I tried, it worked well to compile the paper locally.

Shreyas pointed out recently that (some forum which posts CS papers) does not accept XeLaTeX yet; I am only flagging this to indicate that the world still has not quite caught up with XeLaTeX (on the other hand I am certainly encouraging anyone who asks me to use minted).
fpvandoorn/carleson#535 has been updated. Some remaining comments IMO can be upgraded to final editing tasks.
#579 (by Sébastien) covers items 8e, 9a and 9c
And I'm not sure where the overall assignment for task 16 comes from, is that a typo? @María Inés de Frutos Fernández
Ah thanks, that was a typo, it's now fixed. 16a is done, 16b is still unclaimed.
Task 17a (which I am currently assigned to) seems to be a duplicate of task 13. I think it should just be removed?
Good question! I'm not sure what we originally meant when writing this down, but you might be right.

If I remember correctly, point 17a was meant to cover the fact that we started the project trying to use Real wherever possible, and later on we made the switch to ENNReal, and the changes this required.
13 is more focused on how we dealt with having to use NNReal, Real and ENNReal, in which circumstances to use each one, etc.
The tasks could potentially be combined, but in that case 13 would need to be extended.
fpvandoorn/carleson#582 completes tasks 17a and 17b.
stab at Task 10 following discussions: fpvandoorn/carleson#583
